description: Since defk-jaj a kernel call is inlined, so generated code grows with the number of call sites along every call chain (a diamond-shaped call graph doubles per level). Decide on a limit: count inlined nodes per entry kernel and warn or error past a threshold with a message naming the chain, and/or measure compile time and .so size for a deep/wide call graph. Document the result in README known limitations.

comments.text: Classified nice to have (not a safety gap, not required for the verdict) by 'Which open runtime issues are safety gaps?' (defk-dtw.12).

Triage (defk-sgw plan): needs-triage. The threshold and warn-vs-error choice is undecided. Not required for the verdict ('Which open runtime issues are safety gaps?' ruled it compile-time cost); decide when multi-clause kernels (defk-u9c) and helper kernels make deep call graphs likely.
The 1BRC kernel (defk-n4r.6) inlines parse, hash, probe and compare helpers from several sites; it is the first workload likely to show code-size growth. Record generated C lines and .so size there.

Data point from defk-52v.9 (examples/argon2.exs): argon2's first draft called BLAKE2b's compression at 2 sites per BLAKE2b, BLAKE2b at 3 sites per H', and H' at 2 sites per entry kernel, with two entry kernels (argon2id inlines argon2): 26.6 MB of generated C (224k lines per entry kernel), and clang -O3 had not finished after 10 minutes under load. Rewritten with one call site per helper (each BLAKE2b block copied into a padded buffer; H' as one loop): 3.6 MB of C (29k lines per entry), 1.1 MB .so, ~2.5 min of clang under load, no measurable run-time cost. Recorded as docs/performance.md 6.20. A warning naming the call chain past some inlined-node count would have saved the first 10 minutes.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Warn at compile time when inlining makes an entry kernel's code grow past a threshold, naming the call chain

**Decision (maintainer, triage 2026-10-11):** a compile warning, not an error.

**Current behavior:**
Every kernel call is inlined (defk-jaj), so code size grows with call sites along every chain; a diamond doubles per level. argon2's first draft (helpers called at 2-3 sites per level) produced 26.6 MB of C (224k lines per entry kernel) and clang -O3 had not finished after 10 minutes; one call site per helper gave 29k lines, 1.1 MB .so (docs/performance.md 6.20). Nothing warns.

**Desired behavior:**
- Count inlined size (AST nodes or emitted statements: pick a measure that tracks generated C size) per entry kernel. Past a threshold, emit an Elixir compile warning (IO.warn with the kernel's location) that names the entry kernel, the inlined size, and the call chain(s) that contribute most (e.g. "blake2b inlined 12 times via h_prime -> blake2b"), and suggests one call site per helper (a loop over the inputs, or a buffer).
- Choose the threshold from measurements: measure the measure for every kernel in test/support and examples; the largest legitimate one stays well below, argon2's first draft shape is well above. Record the table and the threshold in docs/performance.md and the language docs' limits/inlining section.
- No effect on code that stays under the threshold; no compile-time cost worth noting (measure).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A test kernel with a diamond call graph several levels deep gets the warning (ExUnit.CaptureIO), naming the chain
- [ ] No warning for any existing test or example kernel (the suite and examples compile with --warnings-as-errors where they did before)
- [ ] Threshold and measurements documented; `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Making it an error; outlining (non-inlined) kernel calls

title: Guard against code-size blowup from inlined kernel calls
